To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the four groups of respondents were very similar in the beliefs they expressed concerning both the causes of alcoholism and means of treating alcoholism.

the beliefs of persons of different sexes, persons differing as to whether they know persons with problem alcohol use, and persons differing as to ethnic background were similar in regard to both the causes of alcoholism and the means of overcoming problem drinking.

The beliefs of different ethnic groups about the causes and treatment of alcohol problems are very similar to one another, and to the beliefs of Caucasians, but the beliefs of Caucasials are different from the beliefs of all other groups in the direction of regarding problem use as more hereditary and as less socially caused."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which persons from different groups share beliefs concerning the causes and cures of alcohol problems.
the extent to which persons of different sexes, ethnic groups, and levels of exposure to problem drinkers share beliefs about the causes of and means of overcoming problem drinking.

the extent to which the beliefs of persons from different ethnic/racial groups and of persons who have been exposed to problem alcohol use differ from those of Caucasians who have not been so exposed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the groups studied here are similar in beliefs regarding the causes of problem alcoholism and the effectiveness of different means of overcoming it, and that the differences that do exist are chiefly between Caucasians and the other groups studied, and that the latter are more likely to attribute problem alcohol use to social factors and to regard the effectiveness of social means of overcoming problem use.
all four groups, regardless of whether they knew problem drinkers, were similar in their beliefs about the causes of alcoholism and the means for overcoming it.

all groups in the study, with only minor differences among them, believed in the importance of social and hereditary causes of problem alcoholism, and in the importance of a wide variety of means of overcoming it, including those which have not been demonstrated as effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are more similarities than differences across ethnic groups in their beliefs about the causes and the treatment of alcohol problems.
there were more similarities than differences in beliefs across the four groups.
all groups have very similar beliefs concerning the causes and treatment of problem alcohol use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a great deal of consensus across ethnic groups regarding the causes and means of treating alcohol problems.

there are few, if any, differences across groups in the causes of problem alcoholism and the effectiveness of treatment, despite the fact that some of our groups differ greatly in their beliefs regarding these matters.

the general public's beliefs about the causes of and means of overcoming problem drinking are similar across ethnic groups and sexes, but that there are some differences between Caucasians and other groups.
